title: Speech and text analytics
summary: What gets transcribed, how sentiment and topics are used, and why analysis is not the same thing as the live conversation.

lessons.title: STA reads the conversation after the channel has it
lessons.summary: Speech and text analytics covers voice and digital interactions. It is not a second ACD.
paras: The overview and the about page describe transcription and analysis of voice interactions and of digital interactions such as email, message, and chat. Voice coverage described there includes the IVR, voice bots, the ACD portion, the agent, conferences, and voicemail. Digital coverage follows the text the customer and the agent already exchanged.

STA is a CX 3-and-above story in the current package overview, because that is where transcription minutes are named. Quality management can exist without it. AI scoring cannot. Do not promise a dialect list or a price from memory. Those tables live on the current pages and they move.
lessons.uncertainty: Confirm dialect coverage and any per-minute price on the current STA pages. This lesson does not list them.

lessons.title: Sentiment is a label on the text, not a mood you can argue with
lessons.summary: Sentiment scores the customer’s language. Use it as a filter, then listen.
paras: The STA pages describe sentiment so you can find interactions that went badly or well without listening to all of them. A negative label is a queue for a human, not a fact about the customer’s life. Sarcasm, a product name that sounds negative, and a language the model handles poorly will all fool a score.

Quality forms and coaching still need the recording or the transcript. Sentiment does not replace the form from the quality track. The FAQ is also where AI scoring’s prerequisites are written. Sentiment by itself does not spend that story.

lessons.title: Topics, programs, and phrases are the dictionary
lessons.summary: A program groups topics. A topic is phrases you expect to hear or read.
paras: The STA overview describes topics and programs so you can find whether a phrase occurred: a competitor, a cancel request, a required disclosure. Phrases are the dictionary. If the phrase is not in the topic, the program will not find it, even when every agent said it.

Start with a few phrases a supervisor can recite. A program with hundreds of unreviewed topics becomes a second language nobody maintains. Content search, in the next lesson, is how you test a phrase before you trust the topic.

lessons.title: Agent empathy is a detected behavior, still a form question
lessons.summary: Empathy detection points at calls. Calibration still decides what empathy means for your company.
paras: The STA material describes agent empathy as something you can detect and later filter on, including for process-automation style triggers when the current article lists that filter. It is a model’s reading of the agent’s language. Your quality form may define empathy differently: a pause, a repeated question, an offer.

Use the detection to find calls for calibration. Do not let the model become the form. Two evaluators who disagree should score the same transcript, which is the calibration practice from the quality track.
lessons.uncertainty: Confirm the current trigger filters on the STA pages before you automate anything from empathy.

lessons.title: Content search is how you test the dictionary
lessons.summary: Search the transcript before you trust a topic count.
paras: The STA pages describe content search so you can find interactions by what was said or written. Use it when a topic count looks wrong. Search the phrase. If search finds it and the topic does not, the dictionary is the bug. If search does not find it, the words were never in the transcript: wrong leg, transcription off, or people said something else.
Search is also how a supervisor prepares a calibration set without guessing. Pull the interactions, then open them in quality management. Do not export customer text into a slide.

lessons.title: Full analysis and a faster transcript are different clocks
lessons.summary: Some views wait until the interaction is complete. A lower-latency transcript path is a different API.
paras: The STA FAQ and overview distinguish analysis that completes after the interaction from lower-latency transcript delivery through the Notifications API. A supervisor refreshing a topic count during the call should not expect the final program result. A bot or a process that needs words sooner has to use the path the page documents for that latency, and only the filters the page lists.

Process-automation triggers described alongside STA can filter on topic, sentiment, and empathy when those filters are on the page you open. Audio streaming to an outside processor is a separate design. Re-read before you name the connector. This lab does not invent a streaming vendor.
lessons.uncertainty: AudioHook and other streaming connectors must be confirmed on the current article. This lesson does not rank vendors.
